title: Prepare support and operations
summary: Make sure the people and processes behind the product are ready on day one: who answers questions, who fixes problems and how issues reach the team.

beginner: List the questions and problems users are likely to have, using beta feedback.
Write help content and short guides for support staff.
Agree how support raises issues with the product team, and how fast each type must be handled.
Check any manual steps behind the scenes have people, training and time.
Run a short practice session with support before launch.
intermediate: Prepare help content, support guides and escalation routes.
Agree service levels for each issue type.
Run a readiness review before launch.
experienced: Design support into the product, with self-service help and clear error messages.
Set up a feedback loop so support themes reach the backlog every week.
Plan for peak demand at launch.
Agree ownership of the product in live service.

canDelegateTo.task: Write the help content and support guides
Agree escalation routes and run the readiness review
Map the operational processes behind the product

toolExamples.jira: Set up a service desk queue with categories that match your escalation routes.
toolExamples.confluence: Publish a support knowledge base linked from the help pages.
toolExamples.notion: Keep a launch-week issue log that support and the team both use.

definitionOfDone: Help content and support guides ready
Escalation routes and service levels agreed
pitfalls: Support learning about the launch from users
No route for problems to reach the team
Forgetting the manual work behind the scenes

sources.title: Designing assisted digital support (GOV.UK Service Manual)
